races.title: State Assembly, District 26
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Patrick Ahrens
cands.bio: Democrat who has represented California's Assembly District 26 since December 2024. Previously a Foothill-De Anza Community College District trustee, elected 2018 and board president from December 2021, and a district director for Assemblymember Evan Low. Holds a Master of Public Administration from San José State.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include the Democratic Party of California, California Federation of Labor Unions, California Nurses Association, California Teachers Association, SEIU Local 521, IUOE Local 3, National Union of Healthcare Workers, California Environmental Voters, Equality California, California Young Democrats and YIMBY Action.

2024 campaign-reported endorsers (from his Candidate Connection survey) include Planned Parenthood Advocates Mar Monte, Equality California, Rep. Anna Eshoo, former Rep. Mike Honda, Assemblymember Evan Low, Santa Clara County Sheriff Bob Jonsen and District Attorney Jeff Rosen.

cands.gaps: We found no statements or actions from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, H-1B or immigration enforcement, policing, gun policy, or school choice. We found no documented stance on development limits or land protection beyond his support for building more housing, and no controversies or foreign ties in the pages we had. His campaign Issues page was cut off before the Safety, Climate and Fiscal Responsibility sections, so those positions are not covered. Ballotpedia's list of bills he sponsored did not display, so his legislation is not covered beyond a bill on student truancy mentioned in his Wikipedia entry. We could not confirm which city he was raised in or whether he ever lived outside California; the 'lifelong resident' claim comes from his own survey.

local.label: Roots 100: Ballotpedia lists his birthplace as San Jose, and in his 2024 survey he describes himself as born in the district and a lifelong resident; his campaign site calls him a Silicon Valley native and a Sunnyvale resident, and he attended De Anza College.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

Janice Hahn and managed a 2014 San Jose City Council campaign; holds a Master of Public Administration.

cands.name: Tim Gorsulowsky
cands.bio: Small business owner who founded a San Jose security services company in 1994 that grew to 165 employees. Has not held elected office. Ran for the Elk Grove school board in 2014 and for the California Assembly in 2014, 2016, 2022 and 2026.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed on Ballotpedia include the Republican Party of California and Reform California, along with several online voter guides.
In his 2014 school board race he was endorsed by the Sacramento County Republican Party and the Sacramento Republican Women Federated.

cands.gaps: His birthplace was not found. He has held no elected office, so there are no votes or official actions to report. We found no documented positions on data centers, development, homestead property taxes, foreign or institutional ownership of land, H-1B or immigration enforcement, gun policy, abortion or school choice and teacher pay. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey, so his statements come from a 2022 survey and a 2014 school board website. We found no news coverage of controversies, and no foreign ties.

local.label: Roots 55: Ballotpedia says he grew up in Shreveport, Louisiana and moved to California in 1987 as an adult, about 39 years ago; his birthplace is not given.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Started a San Jose security services company in 1994 that grew to 165 employees and over $4 million in annual revenue, and says he has started several similar companies since. He has never held elected office.
qual.why: Business ownership and management fall in the middle band for this office. He has no legislative service, and no policy or budget career is documented.

back-police-order.evidence: In a 2022 Ballotpedia survey he said that if elected he would change state law to let law enforcement charge criminals and let district attorneys prosecute successfully. He criticized Propositions 47 and 57.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: In the same 2022 survey he said care of State Parks must be a priority to preserve and protect them. He also called for tighter regulation of new construction and of chemicals in air and ground.
